questions.q: How did David feel about Alan at the start of the chapter, as they lay in the wood?
choices: He held him in horror, believing him a murderer
He was grateful to Alan for saving him from the soldiers
He was angry that Alan had left him alone on Mull
He was proud of Alan for punishing the Red Fox

questions.q: David tells Alan, "You and me must twine." What does "twine" mean here?
choices: Part ways
Join together
Run faster
Make peace

questions.q: In Alan's story of the Man and the Good People, what did the man do before he opened the bag?
choices: He prayed to the king of the fairies for help
He stuck his dirk through it
He threw it into the sea in fear
He called out to see who was inside
questions.evidence: he stuck his dirk throughout that poke before he opened it

questions.q: Why did Alan tell David the story of the man and the bag?
choices: To pass the time while the soldiers marched past
To show that thinking the worst of a friend can be a terrible mistake
To explain where the Good People live on the Skerryvore
To frighten David into staying with him in Appin
questions.evidence: you and the man are very much alike

questions.q: What reason did Alan give to show he would not have killed the Red Fox that way?
choices: He had been at James's house all that morning
He would never kill in his own country, or carry only a fishing-rod
He had promised Ardshiel never to harm a Campbell
He was too far away and could not shoot that far
questions.evidence: if I were going to kill a gentleman, it would not be in my own country

questions.q: How did Alan swear that he had no part in the killing?
choices: On his father's grave in Appin
On the Holy Iron of his dirk
On a Bible from the brig
On the silver button
questions.evidence: I swear upon the Holy Iron

questions.q: When Alan says the murderer's coat was blue and that he was "tying my brogues," what can you tell?
choices: Alan truly did not see the man at all
Alan is avoiding saying who the man was
Alan thinks David himself fired the shot
Alan is sure the man was a Campbell
questions.evidence: I've a grand memory for forgetting, David

questions.q: Why did Alan say he drew the soldiers after himself and David?
choices: So that the real shooter could escape into the heather
So that the soldiers would arrest the Campbell lawyer instead
So that David would be forced to come along with him
So that the soldiers would grow tired and give up the hunt
questions.evidence: the best place for him will be the heather

questions.q: What did David decide about Alan's way of thinking?
choices: His morals were back to front, but he would die for them
His morals were just the same as any good Lowland minister's
He had no morals at all and could not be trusted
He was only pretending to have morals to fool David
questions.evidence: Alan's morals were all tail-first; but he was ready to give his life for them

questions.q: Where did Alan say the trial for the Red Fox's murder would be held?
choices: In Edinburgh, before the Lords of the high court
In Inverara, the Campbells' head place
In Fort William, by the army
In London, before King George
questions.evidence: it'll be tried in Inverara, the Campbells' head place

questions.q: What was Alan's main point about the trial David would face?
choices: That the judges would be fair because the Duke was honest
That a jury of Campbells would surely hang him
That David would be set free since he was a Lowlander
That no trial could be held without a witness
questions.evidence: with fifteen Campbells in the jury-box

questions.q: Why was David more willing to flee once Alan said they were heading "to the Lowlands"?
choices: He wanted to get back and get the upper hand of his uncle
He hoped to find Mr. Campbell and hide in his house
He knew there were no soldiers at all in the Lowlands
He wanted to take a ship from Leith to the American colonies
questions.evidence: I was growing impatient to get back and have the upper-hand of my uncle

questions.q: What choice did Alan say David had?
choices: Go home by sea, or stay in Appin
Take to the heather with him, or hang
Give himself up, or hide in the house of James
Fight the soldiers, or run to Mull
questions.evidence: Either take to the heather with me, or else hang

questions.q: Why did Alan plan to go to Aucharn before fleeing?
choices: To get his clothes, arms and money from James
To warn the tenants that the soldiers were coming
To tell James that the Red Fox was dead
To leave a message for the crew of the brig
questions.evidence: where I must get my clothes, and my arms, and money to carry us along

questions.q: In Alan's account, what happened to the brig Covenant after the crew got into the skiff?
choices: It broke apart and washed ashore in pieces
It lifted over the reef and sank into the sea
It drifted off and was found by a King's cruiser
It stayed stuck on the reef for many days
questions.evidence: the sea closed over the Covenant of Dysart

questions.q: What did Hoseason order the sailors to do once they were on the beach?
choices: Search the shore for David
Lay hands upon Alan
Build a fire and rest
Row back to the wreck
questions.evidence: bade them lay hands upon Alan

questions.q: Who took Alan's side against the other sailors on the beach?
choices: Captain Hoseason
Mr. Riach
Mr. Shuan
The cabin boy
questions.evidence: Riach! Well, it was him that took up the clubs for me

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: David and Alan fighting and parting ways for good
David coming to trust Alan again and agreeing to flee with him
Alan going back to Mull to look for the sailors
Alan and David being tried for the murder in Inverara
